study_identification_part.si_4_title: Nomograms of human hippocampal volume shifted by polygenic scores

dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.detail: UK Biobank (UKB) was the primary dataset used for building normative models (nomograms) of hippocampal volume using Gaussian process regression. 39,664 subjects were initially obtained; after exclusions for neurological/psychiatric conditions, genetic ancestry (non-British), and HV outliers, 35,686 healthy subjects aged 44-82 remained. ADNI was used as an independent external application/evaluation dataset; 1,001 subjects initially, with 818 remaining after exclusions for genetic ancestry and HV quality scores, comprising cognitively normal (CN), mild cognitive impairment (MCI), and Alzheimer's disease (AD) participants.
dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.supporting_text: "Using imaging data from 35,686 healthy subjects aged 44-82 from the UK Biobank (UKB), we built HV nomograms using Gaussian process regression (GPR)" ... "Clinical impact of genetically adjusted nomograms was investigated by comparing 818 subjects from the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI) database diagnosed as either cognitively normal (CN), having mild cognitive impairment (MCI) or Alzheimer's disease (AD) patients."
dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.location: Janahi2022.pdf.md: Abstract, L41; Materials and methods / Datasets, L218-L220

answer.UK Biobank: normative model training (building HV nomograms via GPR from healthy subjects)

dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.detail: The UK Biobank dataset (35,686 healthy subjects) was used exclusively to train the GPR normative models and to generate genetically adjusted nomograms via PGS stratification. The ADNI dataset (818 subjects with CN, MCI, AD diagnoses) was used for external evaluation: testing whether genetically adjusted nomograms improved diagnostic separation, and for longitudinal analysis of MCI-to-AD conversion.
dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.supporting_text: "The UKB dataset was used to train the models and the ADNI dataset was used to test them." ... "In the ADNI dataset we investigated whether the shift in genetically adjusted nomograms could be leveraged for improved diagnosis."

dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.detail: A single normative model was built using Gaussian process regression (GPR) from 35,686 healthy UK Biobank subjects (after excluding 453 for neurological/psychiatric conditions, 3,497 for genetic ancestry, and 28 as HV outliers from the original 39,664). The entire 35,686 healthy subjects served as the training set; there was no internal train/validation/test split. ADNI was used as an entirely separate external evaluation dataset. Genetically adjusted nomograms used subsets (top/bottom 30% by PGS) of these same 35,686 subjects, but the base normative model used all 35,686.

"The UKB dataset was used to train the models and the ADNI dataset was used to test them."

dc_4_age_info_of_each_normative_nodel.detail: The age range of the 35,686 healthy UK Biobank subjects used for the normative model is 44-82 years. The paper states 'aged 44-82' in both the abstract and the Methods section. However, the mean, SD, median, and IQR are not reported. No separate train/test split exists (all 35,686 used as training), so overall-phase and train-phase are identical. The GPR nomograms were generated for ages 45-82 (by increments of 0.25 years), although the data range was 44-82.

dc_5_sex_info_of_each_normative_nodel.detail: The sex breakdown of the 35,686 healthy subjects used for the normative model is not explicitly reported after exclusions. The original UKB sample before exclusions comprised 39,664 subjects (18,718 female, i.e., 47.2% female; 20,946 male, i.e., 52.8% male), but after removing 3,978 subjects (453 for conditions, 3,497 for genetic ancestry, 28 as outliers), the sex breakdown of the remaining 35,686 is not stated. The paper built separate nomograms for males and females, but did not report the exact N per sex in the final sample.
